orig_title: Trucker who crashed off Pascagoula River Bridge identified, cause still unknown
summary: A tractor-trailer driver, identified as 64-year-old Norberto Barahona-Mejia of Conroe, Texas, died after his truck left the Pascagoula River Bridge on I-10 in Jackson County, Mississippi, on November 17. According to a report citing WKRG, the crash happened around 12:15 a.m., after the truck collided with a Honda Accord that was also eastbound, and the trailer went over the side of the bridge into the water below. The 27-year-old driver of the Honda Accord and a 28-year-old passenger were injured and are expected to make full recoveries. Officials are still investigating, and the cause has not been released.

title: Bot Auto launches ‘Capacity Grid’ with agreements for 200 million miles of driverless trucking
orig_title: Bot Auto launches ‘Capacity Grid’ with agreements for 200 million miles of driverless trucking
summary:
Bot Auto has launched Capacity Grid, a network intended to match shipper and broker demand with driverless trucking capacity, and has signed agreements covering 200 million miles of driverless freight operations. Customers can reserve capacity for set routes and time windows at agreed prices, buying transportation by the mile without owning trucks. FreightVana, a logistics company specializing in power-only freight transportation, has a commitment covering 50 million miles.

The company said a driverless load ran from northeast Houston to Hutchins, near Dallas, on April 29, covering 231 miles for Ryan Transportation. Figures reported by the company put the driverless trip at $1.89 per mile, against $3.78 for a comparable human-driven operation within its business. Bot Auto has not specified when the full 200 million miles will be completed.

title: 13 suspects charged in $22M freight train cargo theft scheme in US
orig_title: 13 suspects charged in $22M freight train cargo theft scheme in US
summary: Thirteen men were charged Thursday over an alleged freight train theft operation that prosecutors say took more than $22 million in cargo bound for major retailers. A federal indictment unsealed the same day says the suspects targeted more than 36 trains carrying Nike sneakers, Crocs footwear and power tools that came through the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. Prosecutors allege the group disabled trains by damaging their braking systems at set locations, then moved the goods onto trucks. The merchandise was sold to an unidentified company that allegedly resold it. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli called the alleged thefts "staggering" and promised further prosecutions in similar cases. All 13 defendants face conspiracy and theft of interstate railroad cargo charges, and two of them also face a count involving violence against railroad carriers. If convicted, they could face federal prison terms of five to 20 years.

title: At least 36 Southern California trains burglarised in $22.5 million cargo theft racket; 14 accused allege
orig_title: At least 36 Southern California trains burglarised in $22.5 million cargo theft racket; 14 accused allege
summary:
The US Department of Justice said 14 people have been indicted over alleged thefts of more than $22.5 million in cargo from freight trains in Southern California. According to the DOJ, the group burglarised at least three dozen trains between February 2024 and August 2026, taking goods that included Nike sneakers and Milwaukee tools. Investigators allege members cut air hoses to force emergency stops, then boarded the trains and removed valuable cargo.

Thirteen of the 14 defendants were arrested on Thursday, and the case is a 17-count federal indictment. Investigators allege two defendants sold thousands of pairs of stolen Nike sneakers to a Los Angeles resale business, receiving approximately $1,081,493 between May and October 2025. The alleged leader is identified as Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, of East Los Angeles. All defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

title: Truck driver arrested after he was caught hauling oversized load at night with no permit and suspended CDL, Missouri sheriff says
orig_title: Truck driver arrested after he was caught hauling oversized load at night with no permit and suspended CDL, Missouri sheriff says
summary: A Platte County Sheriff's Office deputy in Missouri arrested a truck driver after stopping an oversized load on I-29 at night without warning devices or banners. The deputy found the driver's commercial driver license suspended and no oversized load permit from the Missouri Department of Transportation, and the load was reported to be over 13 feet wide. The inspection also recorded eight Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulation violations, and the Louisiana for-hire motor carrier and driver were placed out of service. Two days after the driver posted bond, the same deputy stopped the same load on Route 92. This time it had warning devices and banners, but still no MoDOT permit, and 15 violations were recorded. A court summons was issued, and the driver was helped to obtain a permit.

summary: Dallas College and Goodwill Dallas have teamed up with FleetForce Truck Driver Training to widen CDL instruction across Dallas-Fort Worth. The program covers Class A, B and C licenses and combines classroom work with hands-on training, with FleetForce instructors teaching at Goodwill facilities. The Dallas location is FleetForce's 17th in the U.S. The company's Next10,000 campaign aims to train 10,000 students through 2026 and cites about 6,100 local CDL openings in the region. Qualified graduates are guaranteed an interview with a large full-truckload carrier through FleetForce's Pre-Hire network. The article does not yet give enrollment figures or completion and placement rates for Dallas students.

title: Unsafe truck drivers could be publicly outed under new Alberta law
orig_title: Unsafe truck drivers could be publicly outed under new Alberta law
summary: Alberta's government is proposing Bill 43, the Safe and Sensible Roads Act, which would amend the province's Traffic Safety Act to toughen penalties for unsafe trucking. Under the bill, fines for unsafe commercial truck operators would rise from $10,000 to $50,000 for violations including repeated safety breaches and bridge strikes. Driver licences could also be cut to a basic Class 5 licence or made subject to conditions after serious incidents such as a bridge strike. Transportation Minister Devin Dreeshen said retraining would be required before a driver returns to regular duties. If the bill passes, the government would publish information on non-compliant carriers, drivers, driving schools, inspection facilities and company owners and directors. Separately, a Calgary Police Service blitz in September pulled 100 of 197 stopped commercial vehicles off the road for critical defects. In March, a truck hauling equipment struck a rail bridge in Lethbridge, knocking concrete loose and leading to costly repairs for the municipality.

orig_title: Descartes, Highway and Carrier411: The Technology Behind Freight Fraud Prevention
summary: Logistics Viewpoints argues that freight fraud prevention depends on whether a carrier's verified identity holds from contract through physical pickup. It points to an October 2026 Transport Topics examination that described companies including Descartes and Highway connecting identity verification to tracking intelligence and carrier enrollment. The article also cites Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration warnings about broker and carrier identity theft, along with advice to check registration information and watch for suspicious contact changes. It recommends independent confirmation of high-risk changes, such as a new pickup contact, driver, equipment or payment instructions, made through a known channel rather than the incoming message. It also says a valid operating authority record does not by itself establish who is answering calls or receiving pickup instructions.

sum_problems: Source is a law firm marketing article with promotional content; statistics are presented as the firm's own analysis.
Source notes conflicting September baselines (3,659 vs 3,749) and says they should not be mixed; the summary uses only the 3,749 figure and the October total.

pending_summary:
The Wooley Law Firm reported that Texas recorded 3,927 crashes involving commercial motor vehicles in October 2026, citing TxDOT crash records. Those crashes produced 42 deaths and 1,304 reported injuries, including 146 suspected serious injuries. The firm said the crash count rose about 4.7% from September's 3,749 identifiable records, while reported injuries fell about 2.9%.

Dallas County recorded 372 commercial vehicle crashes, five deaths and 151 injuries, and Dallas city limits had 227 crashes. Within Dallas, Interstate 20 led with 31 crashes, followed by Interstate 35E with 25 and Interstate 30 with 23. The firm cautioned that these are raw counts, not rates adjusted for traffic volume or miles traveled.

Prosecutors say the crew hit at least 36 freight trains between February 2024 and August 2026, cutting air hoses to force them to stop. Prosecutors identified Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, of East Los Angeles, as the alleged leader, operating with his father and two uncles. Officials said a Los Angeles-based sneaker resale business, which was not an authorized Nike reseller, bought stolen sneakers and generated more than $1 million for the crew. The defendants are presumed innocent, and the maximum penalties include five years for conspiracy and 10 years for each theft count.

summary: The Department of Transportation (TxDOT) has spoken out about truck drivers striking overpasses in Texas. The column recalls an October semi crash into the I-27 overpass in Lubbock, where the driver misjudged the height, and cites a Houston bridge that has been hit 16 times since January 2025. TxDOT also identified 61 instances of unreported bridge damage so far in 2026. The writer lists improperly measured vehicle height, misunderstood clearance postings and ignored warning signs as common causes, and notes that oversized trucks need permits because some roads and bridges are not designed for them. The writer advises drivers to know their vehicle's height and take another route if a bridge looks like a close fit.

title: Scottsbluff County Highway 71 Crash Kills Two Truck Drivers
orig_title: Scottsbluff County Highway 71 Crash Kills Two Truck Drivers
summary:
Two semi drivers died after their trucks collided head-on on Highway 71, north of Lake Minatare Road, outside Scottsbluff, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at about 9:10 a.m., according to authorities. The northbound driver was identified as 66-year-old Wesley Barkell of Pine Bluffs, Wyoming, and the southbound driver as 38-year-old Robert Henderson of Hemingford, Nebraska. The crash happened in foggy conditions. Three other vehicles drove into the scene and were damaged by debris before emergency crews arrived, but their occupants were uninjured.

Highway 71 was shut down in the area for about nine hours. The Nebraska State Patrol is conducting a full crash reconstruction, including post-crash inspections of both commercial vehicles, and no cause for the collision has been released.

sum_evidence.quote: Four people have been charged, and two are wanted
Six people were allegedly trafficking the stolen vehicles to transportation companies operating in the GTA and elsewhere in North America.
Officers seized 17 stolen and/or re-vinned tractors and 20 stolen and/or re-vinned 53-foot trailers
Police say many of the vehicles had been altered with new decals and stickers.
Both men are encouraged to seek legal counsel and turn themselves in.

sum_problems: The charge lists for the four arrested men are empty in the source, so the specific charges are not stated.
Gurlal Singh appears twice: charged at age 30 and wanted at age 35. The summary names only the wanted Gurlal Singh and does not say whether they are the same person.
The summary says 'Brampton, Ont.', but the source gives only 'Brampton'. Province is inferred from the Toronto-area context and should be checked.
pending_summary: Four men from Brampton, Ont., have been charged and two more are wanted in an alleged theft and trafficking network for tractors, trailers and other heavy equipment in the Greater Toronto Area. York Regional Police said the investigation, called Project Nashville, started in August 2026 with the Auto Cargo Theft Unit and involved six people allegedly selling stolen semi-tractors and 53-foot trailers to transportation companies in the GTA and elsewhere in North America. On Oct. 7, officers executed a search warrant at a commercial trucking yard in Brampton and seized 17 stolen or re-vinned tractors and 20 stolen or re-vinned 53-foot trailers, valued at an estimated $3.6 million combined. Police said many vehicles had new decals and stickers. Gurlal Singh, 35, and Preetam Rattan, 32, are wanted, and police urged both to seek legal counsel and turn themselves in.

title: Three supply chain trends carriers should watch heading into 2027
orig_title: Three supply chain trends carriers should watch heading into 2027
summary: In a FleetOwner column, the chief executive of a Lincoln, Nebraska freight brokerage outlines three supply chain trends he expects fleet owners to watch in 2027. He cites Bureau of Labor Statistics data showing that trucking has lost more than 100,000 jobs since 2023, although the decline slowed in 2026. Using mileage and fuel-economy figures from the American Transportation Research Institute and Department of Energy diesel prices from early 2026 onward, he estimates that higher diesel costs add roughly $40,000 a year per truck, or $400,000 for a 10-truck fleet. He warns that if a recession pushed rates below operating costs, some carriers would be forced to haul freight at a loss. He also argues that driver shortages will keep pressure on pay, which fuel costs make harder to fund.

title: Einride Says Contracted Revenue Grew 76% to $167 Million
orig_title: Einride Says Contracted Revenue Grew 76% to $167 Million
summary: Einride, the Swedish autonomous and electric freight company listed on Nasdaq as ENRD, said its contracted annual recurring revenue was about $167 million as of November 2026, up 76% from $95 million at the end of June. In a third-quarter business update issued November 18, 2026, it reported constant currency revenue of SEK 185.9 million ($18.3 million), a 27% rise from the second quarter. The company said it has added eight customers since June, bringing its total to more than 40. Its two cab-less electric trucks for EASE Logistics went into daily freight operations in Marysville, Ohio, in September. The company reaffirmed second-half 2026 revenue guidance of $39-42 million, but its adjusted EBITDA outlook for that period was widened to negative $39 to 41 million.

title: FMCSA seeks input on using cameras in place of truck mirrors
orig_title: FMCSA seeks input on using cameras in place of truck mirrors
summary: FMCSA has opened a public comment period on a request to let fleets use Safety Vision's View Smart cameras instead of the two side mirrors required on commercial trucks and buses. A notice published Nov. 18 in the Federal Register says Safety Vision is seeking a five-year exemption from the rule requiring a rear-vision mirror on each side, and the agency has not approved the request. The system uses weatherproof cameras on both sides that feed video to screens mounted along the windshield, which the company says offers a wider view, better low-light visibility and alerts for nearby pedestrians or vehicles. Safety Vision has supplied the system to transit bus operators since 2024, though those buses still carry their required mirrors. FMCSA will weigh the application, safety analyses and public comments before deciding whether the system offers safety equal to conventional mirrors. Comments are accepted at Regulations.gov through Dec. 18 under docket FMCSA-2026-3707.

title: Big rig's brake failure blamed for 'airborne' rotor that killed motorist on I-84, Connecticut troopers say
orig_title: Big rig's brake failure blamed for 'airborne' rotor that killed motorist on I-84, Connecticut troopers say
summary:
Connecticut State Police are investigating a fatal crash in Tolland that involved a semi truck's brake rotor. Troopers responded to a reported incident on westbound I-84 near Exit 69 around 12:45 p.m. on November 18. Investigators said Juan Marty Del Toro was driving a 2014 Nissan NV200 west when a 2019 Kenworth truck operated by Manpreet Singh was eastbound nearby.

Police said the Kenworth suffered a brake failure that caused rotors to come apart and become airborne. One rotor hit the Nissan, came through the windshield and struck Marty Del Toro, who was pronounced dead at the scene. A passenger was taken to a hospital for evaluation. Police asked anyone with additional information or dash cam video to come forward.

title: Commercial Driver's License: Saia LTL Freight; Application for Exemption
orig_title: Commercial Driver's License: Saia LTL Freight; Application for Exemption
summary:
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration is asking for public comment on an exemption application from Saia LTL Freight, a company headquartered in John Creek, Georgia. Saia wants commercial learner's permit holders in its driver training program to operate combination vehicles with double trailers while under the direct supervision of a CDL holder with a doubles/triples endorsement. The notice states that it does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach.

Saia has requested a 5-year exemption from two rules, 49 CFR 383.93(b)(1) and 383.37(a). According to the filing, approximately 300 trainees a year would use a fleet of about 19 training vehicles. Comments are due December 18, 2026, under docket FMCSA-2026-2642. After reviewing the application, safety analyses and public comments, FMCSA will either grant or deny the request.

title: Q3 2026 Cargo Theft Falls as Losses Rise
orig_title: Q3 2026 Cargo Theft Falls as Losses Rise
summary:
Verisk CargoNet reported 547 supply chain crime incidents involving cargo across the U.S. and Canada in the third quarter of 2026, down 33% from a year earlier and 19% from the second quarter. Estimated losses still rose 12% to $230.1 million. Fictitious pickups, in which criminals use deception to obtain a shipment, fell only 6% to 138, so their share of reported activity rose to about 25%.

Through September, reported incidents were down 25% year to date, while estimated losses rose 39% to $718.9 million. The average value of stolen goods with a documented value rose 72% to $448,456. CargoNet logged 19 thefts of $1 million or more, compared with nine a year earlier. California accounted for about a third of incidents, and four states made up 57% of the quarterly total. CargoNet also documented fraud schemes in 2026 that used compromised email accounts, internet phone systems and transportation applications, and said theft has historically risen in Q4.

ACT Research said freight demand improved for a third straight month in October and now believes the freight cycle has entered its growth phase. The Cass Freight Index shipments component rose 5.9% year over year in October, up from 1.9% in September, helped by an easy comparison with late-2025 trade war effects. Seasonally adjusted, shipments gained 1.7% month over month.

Expenditures on freight grew 27% year over year to 4.01 in October, from a 20% gain in September, driven by higher shipments, rates and fuel surcharges. The Cass Truckload Linehaul Index reached 156.2, up 0.9% month over month and 9.9% year over year, as both spot and contract rates rose. The source says the near-term direction seems higher still, and that normal seasonality would put November shipments up 3% year over year. Elevated inflation, rising interest rates and the temporary nature of IEEPA tariff refunds are cited as limits on demand.

title: GTCC and Old Dominion Freight Line support future truckers

summary:
Guilford Technical Community College in Greensboro runs a truck driver training program that staff say has grown every year since it started six years ago. The certificate takes eight weeks of full-time study or 14 weeks of nights and weekends, and costs about $1,800 including books. Jan Knox, VP of the college advancement foundation, said graduates can often find work right away at a salary of $60,000 or more.

Old Dominion Freight Line, a trucking company headquartered in the Triad, is funding four $1,000 scholarships a year at the college, two of them for women. Chris Brooks, Senior VP of HR at the company, said the awards help people who might not otherwise afford a CDL or a diesel mechanic certification. The company said it has over 200 women drivers.

title: Higher diesel prices strain farm transportation budgets
orig_title: Higher diesel prices strain farm transportation budgets
summary:
Higher diesel prices are adding costs for Iowa farmers and trucking operators, according to Matt Wells, vice president of the Mid-West Truckers Association. Wells cited refinery shutdowns, declining fuel reserves and the war between Russia and Ukraine as factors tightening supply. He said two California refineries were shut down and a refinery in Joliet, Illinois, was offline for seven to ten days, while Ukrainian attacks damaged Russian refining facilities.

Wells said transportation rates and operating budgets will need to reflect the higher costs, potentially for the next year to year and a half, and he does not expect diesel prices to fall significantly soon. He also cautioned that fuel prices do not always return to earlier levels after a large increase. On red-dyed diesel, Wells said the modern dyed product is essentially the same fuel as clear highway diesel, and that its use on public roads remains subject to federal and state tax requirements and any specifically authorized exemptions.

orig_title: Samsara expands AI fleet management tools, adds voice support for drivers
summary:
Fleet technology provider Samsara has opened its Agent Studio platform to all of its customers, letting trucking companies and other fleet operators build custom AI assistants. According to Samsara, use of its AI agents has grown sevenfold since June 2026, as customers apply them to fuel efficiency analysis, compliance monitoring and driver assistance. The agents can be set to respond to specific events or operating conditions rather than waiting for a user's question.

Samsara says the agents can flag possible hours-of-service violations before they occur by weighing scheduled stops, remaining driving time and shift hours. A voice feature can call a driver when the truck enters a geofence around a distribution center and give site-specific instructions. The company reports that voice interactions overtook chat within four weeks of the feature's launch, and that about 75% of organizations using voice agents have increased weekly usage.

summary:
A federal appeals court in the Second Circuit on November 13 set aside a $73.5 million federal funding penalty against New York over nondomiciled commercial driver's licenses. The court found that federal officials were trying to enforce a licensing requirement that the governing regulations did not contain. Parriva asks whether California can use the same reasoning to challenge its own penalty.

An October 1 Federal Highway Administration notice shows $31,229,953 withheld from California, covering the period October 1 through December 11, 2026. California's separate dispute involves an estimated $158.3 million in fiscal 2027 highway funding, which does not mean that full amount has been withheld. The California case is docketed as No. 26-1027 before the D.C. Circuit and was scheduled for oral argument on September 11, 2026. Parriva said it could not verify a final merits decision as of November 14.

title: Field to Freight: John Deere Connects Farm Production With Renewable Diesel Alternatives
orig_title: Field to Freight: John Deere Connects Farm Production With Renewable Diesel Alternatives
summary:
John Deere is testing 100% biodiesel (B100) in five semi-trucks for six months under its Field to Freight initiative, according to an RFD-TV interview with John Deere Biofuels Director Nate Green. The trucks deliver parts and equipment to dealers and farmers from the company's distribution center in Milan, Illinois, and were fitted with an upgrade kit installed by Optimus Technologies. Penske, CPC Logistics and Chevron are also involved, with Chevron supplying the biodiesel.

The trucks use a dual-tank system to start on diesel and switch to B100 once the engine warms, and they recirculate diesel at shutdown. Green said the demonstration will show whether the technology works within the company's logistics network, and John Deere would consider wider deployment if it does. He also said full life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions from biodiesel can be 50% to 85% lower than petroleum diesel, depending on feedstock.

summary: Two people have been sentenced over an illegal border crossing at the Sprague crossing in Manitoba. The Canada Border Services Agency said it stopped a minivan on May 7 because of "inconsistencies" in the driver's declaration, and officers found a 46-year-old man hiding in the trunk. That man, Temitope Omofuyi Davies, told officers he had paid the driver $1,000 to get him into Canada, and the agency later learned he had also been caught trying to cross near Surrey, B.C., in March. Davies pleaded guilty to failure to report on Aug. 19 and was sentenced to time served. The driver, Annan Nigel Ferguson, a 50-year-old American citizen, was sentenced on Nov. 4 to one year in prison for aiding and abetting failure to report. With time served counted, he has roughly three months left on the sentence.

orig_title: Bain study notes that almost 80% of U.S. fleets plan major truck investments
summary: Bain & Company's 2026 new US Truck Study found that close to 80% of American fleet operators intend to make large equipment investments within six to 12 months. The survey of 210 operators also found that 79% expect fleet growth over the next 12 months, and more than a third of those expect growth of 10% or more. Bain linked the rise in demand to autonomy becoming a central focus and to Tesla expanding its capacity. For truck makers, the report's main point is having units ready to sell, saying availability wins. Fuel efficiency led purchase priorities for 45% of operators, followed by reliability and uptime at 42% and total cost of ownership at 37%. Bain said total cost of ownership has grown in importance and now ranks alongside fuel efficiency at the top.

summary: A wrongful death lawsuit has been filed against Contract Transportation Systems Co. (CTS) and one of its truck drivers over a fatal crash on White Horse Road in Greenville, South Carolina. The complaint was filed Nov. 4 in federal court, on behalf of the estate of Leonard Harding McPeak Jr. The suit alleges that the CTS driver, heading northbound, pulled into a median turn lane and backed the tractor-trailer across southbound lanes while trying to reach a Sherwin-Williams store, so McPeak's pickup struck the trailer on Jan. 7. The plaintiff says McPeak suffered severe injuries and died, and accuses the driver of negligence and of violating South Carolina traffic laws and federal motor carrier safety rules. The suit also accuses CTS of negligent hiring, retention, training and supervision, seeks actual, consequential and punitive damages, and has requested a jury trial.

title: Trucking By the Numbers: Driver stats, for-hire vs private
orig_title: Trucking By the Numbers: Driver stats, for-hire vs private
summary: FleetOwner's annual Trucking By the Numbers feature looks at driver figures for for-hire and private fleets. Citing the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, it puts the number of heavy- and tractor-trailer truck drivers at about 2.2 million in 2025. According to the American Transportation Research Institute, the ratio of drivers to trucks dropped to 0.9 that year, and for-hire annual turnover was about 44.2%, down from 48% in 2024. The article says turnover was highest at the largest truckload fleets, at 70.7%. A National Private Truck Council survey of 89 private fleet respondents reported a 17.1% turnover rate, with about 58% of private fleet drivers able to go home every night. Compared with the ATA annualized salary, the surveyed private fleets paid about 19% higher wages.

Robinson acquired DeSpir on June 22, 2026, and said the deal expanded its network of vetted, security-focused contract carriers. title: Effort to get trucks off Van Dam in Saratoga Springs continues to stall
orig_title: Effort to get trucks off Van Dam in Saratoga Springs continues to stall
summary:
Saratoga Springs residents and city officials are again pushing to move tractor-trailer traffic off Van Dam Street. The push followed a late-night crash between a Skidmore College bus and a tractor-trailer that blocked traffic for hours at Van Dam and Clinton streets, though no major injuries occurred.

A five-ton weight limit ordinance the City Council passed in December 2023 came down within days, because the state said city officials had no authority to pass local ordinances on the state-designated route. A city request for a traffic study outlined rerouting trucks via Route 9 from Northway exit 14 in Malta or via Route 50 through Ballston Spa. The state said de-designating a route requires documented operational deficiencies or a provable history of accidents. A neighborhood association study counted upward of 700 trucks a day, and the Trucking Association of New York warned that de-designation could push trucks onto other routes.

title: NHTSA funding could help truck owners catch safety recalls sooner
orig_title: NHTSA funding could help truck owners catch safety recalls sooner
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Nov. 5 it will provide $1.5 million to help states improve how they notify vehicle owners about open safety recalls. Funded state programs would develop reliable notification methods tied to vehicle registration and renewal, measure how many recalled vehicles get repaired, and document results so other states can adopt successful practices. NHTSA also wants applicants to study how owners respond to different notification methods and track whether repairs follow. The program is not specifically aimed at commercial trucks, but the article notes that better alerts could help carriers and owner-operators plan repairs.
